failure_summary.description: Follow-ups used a stale or overly broad cache result, repeated existing criteria, skipped a needed update, or failed to save the changed result.
A named place was treated as a neighborhood, or an area preference was incorrectly sent to proximity search.
A preference for a 3.5-star rating was treated as an exact score rather than a minimum.
The agent retrieved and re-saved a completed hotel result while handling a restaurant-only update.

patch.reasoning: Clarify how to select and update the appropriate cached base without replaying constraints or touching satisfied deliverables. Make the proximity decision depend on whether the phrase names an area or a venue anchor, and distinguish a star-rating threshold from an explicitly exact score.

edits.target: If a suitable cached base exists and a new constraint is not reflected in it, retrieve the latest suitable result using `get_results_from_cache(key="<exact key from the cache summary>")` and assign the returned result; do not rely on variables from earlier code or turns. Apply only the new same-domain filter and save the update under a fresh relevant key.
edits.content: For an unmet deliverable with a new constraint, use the latest suitable cache result in the same domain, location, and itinerary leg that already reflects all prior constraints still in force; this may be a combined nearest result. Retrieve it by its exact key into a variable in this turn, apply one same-domain filter with only the new constraint(s), and save the exact output under a fresh key. Do not fall back to a broader base, replay prior filters, rely on earlier-turn variables, or process and re-save unrelated deliverables already satisfied.

edits.target: - **Use proximity tools only for proximity requests:**
edits.content: **Resolve the proximity referent first:** If “near X” names an area or district, use X as a `neighborhood` constraint; do not call `search_nearest`. If X names a venue or landmark, identify its supported domain, retrieve or search for that anchor result, and pair it with results for the requested target domain in `search_nearest`; pass exactly two distinct domain inputs and set `groupBy` to the target domain. Do not put a venue name in `neighborhood` or call `search_nearest` with a missing input.

edits.target: For ratings, treat a single numeric rating without minimum or “at least” language as exact `[x, x]`; “exactly x” is `[x, x]`, and an explicit “at least x” request is `[x, 5]`.
edits.content: For ratings, interpret phrases such as “a [x]-star rating” or “[x]-star-rated” as a minimum `[x, 5]` unless the user says “exactly x”; an unqualified numeric rating or score (for example, “rating 4”) is exact `[x, x]`, and “at least x” is `[x, 5]`.
